messages:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need final acceptance criteria for the PRD on graceful degradation for text-generation endpoints. Launch gating depends on these.
Kevin Patel: Can you list the must-haves? latency targets, error budget, fallback behavior, monitoring.
Maria Chen: High level: 1) latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) per route class, 2) error-budget + escalation rules, 3) deterministic fallback chain (degraded model, reduced context, cache), 4) observability + QA prompt suites.
Sasha Ilyin: Propose concrete SLO numbers so eng can bake tests. My draft: Class A (interactive single-turn) P95 <= 350ms, P99 <= 800ms; Class B (multi-turn chat) P95 <= 800ms, P99 <= 2s; Embeddings P95 <= 200ms.
Pradeep Rao: Those look reasonable for nominal load. Need tiered SLOs for peak vs baseline and per-region variance. Also include token-length buckets (<256, 256-1024, >1024).
Maria Chen: Agreed. PRD will define route classes + token buckets. For launch gating we require baseline + peak synthetic checks.
Kevin Patel: Draft fallback chain (ordered):
```
1) Same model with reduced max_tokens + aggressive batching
2) Quantized/INT8 variant on same architecture
3) Smaller distilled model compatible with the API
4) Deterministic cached response for exact prompt matches
5) 503 with client guidance when no fallback possible
```
Sasha Ilyin: Streaming edge-case: if we lose streaming capability, prefer falling back to final non-streaming response instead of 503 to preserve UX. Add header semantics.
Maria Chen: Acceptance criterion for streaming: if streaming failure rate > 1% over 10m window, fallback to non-streaming final responses for that route instance.
Pradeep Rao: Observability requirements: per-route token/latency histograms, error budget burn rate alerts, 10 probes/min/region synthetic checks, and probe-based SLO reporting.
Kevin Patel: API contract: on fallback return 200 with metadata flag, never silently degrade. Header: `X-Redwood-Degraded: <reason>` and `X-Redwood-Fallback-Model: <id>` when applicable. 503 only if chain exhausted.
Sasha Ilyin: Safety filter behavior: if content is blocked, we should avoid 200 + blank. Proposal: return 422 with block reason and remediation link, and emit analytics event for every block.
Maria Chen: PRD decision: 422 for safety blocks + analytics event. Include standard remediation URL in body.
Pradeep Rao: Rollout/runbook: canary at 1% traffic for 24h with synthetic probes and health checks. Rollback if any P0 or if error budget burn > 50% in 24h.
Kevin Patel: QA plan: prompt set per route class (100 prompts each) to measure quality delta of fallback models. Threshold: <= 5% degradation on primary metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim as appropriate).
Sasha Ilyin: I'll add fallback headers, streaming fallback flow, and API examples to the RFC this afternoon. @Pradeep can you own canary config + alerts?
Pradeep Rao: On it. I'll stub out Prometheus alerts, PagerDuty escalation, and the rollback job.
OpsBot: deploy-checklist: canary window alert configured, synthetic probes enabled, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/graceful-degrade
Maria Chen: Next steps — Sasha updates RFC/PRD, Kevin updates acceptance test plan, Pradeep finalizes canary. Reconvene tomorrow 10:00am PT to sign off. :thumbsup:
